anomalies.observed: Net /NET0099 connects only the anodes of D7, D11, and D35; it has no connection to any supply rail or driver.
anomalies.expected: The common anode net should be tied to a positive supply rail (e.g., +3V3) so the LEDs can be driven by their cathode-side resistors.
anomalies.impact: D7, D11, and D35 cannot illuminate; the intended status/activity indication is lost.

anomalies.observed: R73 is connected between D16 pin 2 (K2) and NET0177, which is also D16 pin 4 (A2). This places R73 in parallel with the LED.
anomalies.expected: R73 should be in series with the LED, typically from D16 pin 2 (K2) to GND, to limit current when NET0177 drives the anode.
anomalies.impact: The second LED in dual LED D16 is bypassed and will not light; the intended indicator function is lost.

anomalies.observed: The isolated-side ground pins GND2 of U13 and U16 are connected directly to the main GND net. Their VCC2 pins are also powered from 5V_switched_CAN, which is derived from the main +5V rail.
anomalies.expected: For isolated CAN buses, GND2 and VCC2 should be on an isolated ground/power domain, separate from the main GND and +5V rails.

evidence.quote: two isolated CAN buses (CAN0, CAN1), each driven by its own MCP2515 SPI CAN controller ... through an isolated CAN transceiver

anomalies.impact: Galvanic isolation of the CAN buses is defeated, so ground loops and common-mode noise can couple between the rover electronics and motor controllers; the isolation barrier provides no protection.
